title: Little Office of S. Anna
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.english: Jesus, Mary, Anne.
℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.
℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto, Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
Hymn

blocks.source: O gloriosa Domina, De cujus Virgo genere Coeli Regem columen Laetavit sacro ubere.
blocks.english:
O glorious lady,
Of whose line the Virgin
Gladdened the King, the support of heaven,
At her holy breast.

blocks.source: Quod Eva tristis abstulit, Redditur Patri Filiae, Quae sancta sanctis procreat, Coeli fenestra facta est.
blocks.english:
What sorrowful Eve took away
Is restored to the Father of the Daughter.
She who brings forth holy things for the holy
Has become a window of heaven.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints “Redditur Patri Filiae”, literally “is restored to the Father of the Daughter”. This difficult reading is retained in Latin and translated literally pending editorial resolution.

blocks.source: Tu Regis alti gratiam Deposce, atque veniam, Memoriam colentibus Tuae perennis gloriae.
blocks.english:
Ask the grace of the King on high
And His pardon
For those who honour the memory
Of thine everlasting glory.

blocks.source: Gloria tibi, Domine, Ex Anna natae germine, Cum Patre et Sancto Spiritu, In saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english:
Glory be to Thee, O Lord,
Born from the offspring of Anne,
With the Father and the Holy Ghost,
For ever and ever. Amen.
Antiphon

blocks.source: Coeleste beneficium introivit in Annam, ex qua nobis nata est B. V. Maria.
blocks.english: A heavenly blessing entered into Anne, of whom the Blessed Virgin Mary was born unto us.
℣. Pray for us, Saint Anne.
℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
Let us pray,

blocks.source: Deus, qui beatae Annae tantam gratiam conferre dignatus es, ut Genetricis unigeniti Filii tui mater effici mereretur: concede propitius, ut cujus memoriam veneramur in terris, ejus apud te patrociniis adjuvemur in coelis. Per eundem Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate Spiritus Sancti Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: O God, who didst deign to confer such grace upon blessed Anne that she merited to become the mother of the Mother of Thine only-begotten Son: graciously grant that we who venerate her memory on earth may be helped by her patronage with Thee in heaven. Through the same our Lord Jesus Christ, Thy Son, who liveth and reigneth with Thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end. Amen.

blocks.source: Clara diei gaudia Modulizat Ecclesia, In Annae Christi famula Pandens caeli miracula.
blocks.english:
The Church sings the bright joys of this day,
Revealing the wonders of heaven
In Anne, the handmaid of Christ.

blocks.source: Gloria tibi, Domine, Ex Anna natae germine, Cum Patre et Sancto Spiritu, In saecula saeculorum. Amen.

blocks.source: Alma Regum progenies, Et Sacerdotum soboles, Stirpem illustrum Patribus Suis ornavit actibus.
blocks.english:
Noble offspring of kings
And descendant of priests,
She adorned the lineage of illustrious fathers
By her deeds.

blocks.source: Nupta, Dei judicio, Fideli matrimonio, Juxta verbum angelicum Fructum concepit coelicum.
blocks.english:
Married by the judgment of God
In faithful wedlock,
According to the angelic word
She conceived heavenly fruit.

blocks.source: In saecula pro tempore, Prope marcescens corpore; Decreto Patris luminum Parit Reginam Virginum.
blocks.english:
Advanced in age with the passing of time,
Her body almost withered,
By decree of the Father of lights
She brings forth the Queen of virgins.

blocks.source: Anna pia mater ave, Cujus nomen est suave: Anna sonat gratiam.
blocks.english:
Hail, Anne, loving mother,
Whose name is sweet:
Anne signifies grace.

blocks.source: Ave Jesse radix florens, Quae coelestes das odores, Perenem fragrantiam.
blocks.english:
Hail, flowering root of Jesse,
Who givest heavenly scents,
An enduring fragrance.

blocks.source: Ave patens stella maris, Quam tu nuptam contemplaris Regis regum Filio.
blocks.english:
Hail, shining star of the sea,
Whom thou beholdest espoused
To the Son of the King of kings.
blocks.editorialNote: The stanza addresses the star of the sea, then says “whom thou beholdest espoused to the Son of the King of kings”. Its unusual changes of address are retained rather than rewritten.

blocks.source: Tu, quae sola meruisti Parens esse matris Christi; Preces nostras suscipe:
blocks.english:
Thou who alone didst merit
To be the parent of the Mother of Christ,
Receive our prayers:

blocks.source: Tu nos Matri, atque Patri, Et Reginae Poli Commendare non desine.
blocks.english:
Cease not to commend us
To the Mother and the Father,
And to the Queen of heaven.

blocks.english: Jesus, Mary, Anne.
℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thine anger from us.
℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: Obtentu suae Filiae Mariae plenae gratiae, Nobis auctorem omnium Reddat Anna propitium.
blocks.english:
By the favour of her Daughter,
Mary, full of grace,
May Anne make the Author of all things
Gracious to us.

blocks.source: Has horas canonicas Cum devotione Dixi, sancta Anna, tui ratione; Ut sis mihi praesens mortis in agone, Et vivamus jugiter in caelesti regione.
blocks.english:
These canonical hours I have devoutly said,
Saint Anne, in thy honour;
That thou mayest be present to me in the agony of death,
And that we may live for ever in the heavenly country.
Amen.

editorialNotes.text: All four pages were visually compared. Hymns and the collect have prepared English. Repeated collects display the full prayer from Matins; the seven printed hours exclude Lauds. Two difficult printed hymn readings remain explicit and provisional.
